content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Production Migrations helps operate an application safely outside the developer’s machine. Production readiness requires observable behavior, controlled failure, recovery evidence and safe configuration.

content_blocks.title: What to learn
content_blocks.text: This lesson covers: Migration review; Safe schema-change sequencing; Rollback planning; Coordinating code and schema releases. Keep the source terms intact; for each one, name the component that owns the behavior, the inputs/assumptions, and the expected result.

content_blocks.title: Worked example: Production Migrations
content_blocks.code:
import sqlite3

connection = sqlite3.connect("practice.db")
try:
    connection.execute("CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS tasks (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, title TEXT NOT NULL)")
    connection.execute("INSERT INTO tasks (title) VALUES (?)", ("Review Flask",))
    connection.commit()
    rows = connection.execute("SELECT id, title FROM tasks ORDER BY id").fetchall()
    print(rows)
except Exception:
    connection.rollback()
    raise
finally:
    connection.close()
content_blocks.expected_output: The example creates a local tasks table, inserts one row with a parameterized value, commits on success, rolls back on failure, and closes the connection.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Run in a disposable directory. Delete only the local practice.db file when you want a clean restart; never use production data for this exercise.

content_blocks.title: Before using this beyond practice
content_blocks.text: Validate untrusted input at the server boundary, keep secrets out of source code, and test the failure path. Optional extensions or hosting infrastructure are separate dependencies unless stated otherwise.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a fragment without checking its imports, app configuration or dependencies.
common_mistakes.why: Many Flask examples assume a configured app and a specific runtime or extension version.
common_mistakes.fix: Follow the run instructions, record the Flask/Python version and test the smallest behavior first.

common_mistakes.problem: Checking only the successful request path.
common_mistakes.why: Missing fields, unsupported methods, unauthorized objects and service failures often have different behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Add a negative or boundary test and assert the status code and response contract.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating a local example as production-ready.
common_mistakes.why: Secret management, concurrency, deployment, monitoring and failure recovery need separate design decisions.
common_mistakes.fix: Review the matching deployment and security references before publication or real use.
